title: Create a project
summary: Make a new project with its nine sections from the explorer header, the File menu or the organization menu.
roles: A license (without one you can only view)

title: Rename a project
summary: Rename a project in the tree with F2 or on its data sheet; the name is kept after a reload.
roles: A license and a project role that may edit the project

title: The sections of a project
summary: The nine fixed sections of every project, what each holds and what can be made in it.
roles: Anyone who can open the project

training.topic: The nine sections of a project

title: Hide a project's folders from the tree
summary: Hide folders such as Processes or Branches from the tree, for everyone or for the members of some groups, in every project of the organization or in one project; their objects stay where they are.
roles: Every project: administrators who manage the organization's policies; one project: who may configure the project (Project administrator and above)

title: Rows, clicks and marks in the explorer
summary: What a click, a double-click and the arrow do on each kind of row, and what the marks at the end of a row mean.
roles: Anyone who can open the project

title: Values beside the names: columns in the explorer
summary: Show up to five attributes beside each object's name, so the explorer reads as a tree and a table.
roles: Anyone who can open the project; the columns are your own

title: Folders and 2D spaces inside a project
summary: Make, nest, rename, void and delete folders in any section and 2D spaces in Model Space.
roles: A license and a project role that may edit the project

title: Move rows by drag and drop
summary: Drag 2D spaces, folders, objects and projects in the explorer; drops that do not fit are refused.
roles: A license and a project role that may edit the project

training.topic: Drag and drop in the explorer

title: Search the explorer
summary: Filter the tree as you type and find objects by tag, name, line number or any value (also as a quantity: 24 volt) in all your projects.
roles: Anyone who can open the project

title: The explorer header: expand, collapse and more
summary: The buttons at the top of the explorer: new project, delete, search, Expand all, Collapse all, Retag… and hide.
roles: Everyone

title: Arrange projects in folders, Move up and Move down
summary: Put your projects in personal folders and in your own order; it changes nothing for anyone else.
roles: Everyone (the arrangement is personal)

title: The organization menu and switching organization
summary: The menu on the organization's name: new project, new folder, a query over all projects, and Switch organization.
roles: Everyone

title: Delete a project and restore it from the Bin
summary: A deleted project goes to the Bin, from where it is restored or deleted permanently.
roles: A project role that may delete the project

title: The project Bin: Deleted bin and Voided bin
summary: Restore, delete permanently or empty what was deleted in a project, and unvoid what was voided.
roles: A license and a project role that may edit the project

title: Empty a bin (the permission Empty bins)
summary: Delete everything in a project's Deleted bin, or every project in the workspace's Bin, for good at once; only with the permission Empty bins.
roles: The permission Empty bins in the project (Project administrator has it; a custom role can be given it)

title: Branches
summary: Make a working branch of part of the design, change it while main stays as it is, and push it back when it is ready.
roles: Creating and working in a branch: Engineer and above; pushing to main: Lead engineer and above

title: Pull from main and resolve conflicts
summary: Pull brings main's changes into a branch value by value; what both changed differently is a conflict you resolve, also on the drawing.
roles: Creating and working in a branch: Engineer and above; pushing to main: Lead engineer and above

training.topic: Pull from main and resolve conflicts

title: Push a branch to main
summary: Push brings a branch into the project as one change that undoes as one; it waits until the branch is up to date with main.
roles: Creating and working in a branch: Engineer and above; pushing to main: Lead engineer and above
Setting the types: Project admin; choosing a type: anyone creating a branch
title: Branch types and resolution rules
summary: The project's branch types say whether a branch needs a review before main, what happens after a push, how main's edits treat its objects, and which conflicts settle themselves.

roles: Asking: the branch's members; approving: Lead engineer and above, never the author with four eyes
title: Merge requests: Ask for review
summary: A branch asks for review before it goes to main; a colleague approves or requests changes, and the object shows Under merge review meanwhile.

roles: Creating and working in a branch: Engineer and above; pushing to main: Lead engineer and above
title: Branch packages
summary: Cut part of a branch into a package of its own that can be pushed alone, such as a commissioning package.

roles: Anyone who can work in a branch
title: Alex in a branch and Open as branch
summary: In a branch, Alex and stored assistants change the branch; a held proposal can be kept as a branch with Open as branch.

title: The sample project: Sample E1
summary: Sample E1 is a project template that comes with E1: File → New sample project (Sample E1) gives your own copy in a few seconds of the Demo Field, a fictional oil and gas production facility imported by E1 with the DEXPI reference P&ID, that shows every part of E1 with synthetic data, from the plant breakdown, single line and loop diagrams to workflows, tasks, branches and the status dashboard; delete a copy when you no longer need it.
roles: Everyone in a new organization sees it as its owner made it; adding a copy needs the permissions to create a project and to import data

training.topic: Getting started on the sample project

title: Project templates: save a project as a template, start a project from one
summary: Keep a copy of a project as a template, see the organization's templates in Configuration, and make a new project as a blank one or as a copy of a template.
roles: Saving needs the Export permission in the project and the permission to create projects; making a project from a template needs the permission to create projects; a template is deleted by whoever saved it or an organization administrator

title: History kept: how long a project keeps its change history
summary: Choose in Project settings → History how long the project keeps its change history in History and the change feed; older history moves to the archive, nothing is deleted.
roles: Choosing needs Configure the project (Project administrator); everyone who may view the project sees the setting

title: Import a DEXPI P&ID
summary: Bring a P&ID from another tool into a project as objects, values and a drawing, and import it again later to update what is there, deciding every difference yourself.
roles: The Import data permission in the project (Project administrator and Lead engineer have it) and the permissions of the changes the import makes

training.topic: Importing a P&ID from another tool

title: Export a 2D space as DEXPI
summary: Write a 2D space's pipelines, segments, equipment, instruments and drawing as a DEXPI 2.0 file, for a 3D design tool or another P&ID tool; imported again it gives the same pipelines, segments and boundaries.
roles: The Export permission in the project; no content package licence is needed

training.topic: Handing over a P&ID as DEXPI

title: Import Excel workbooks
summary: Bring tag lists and data sheets from Excel into a project: each sheet becomes a kind of object and each column an attribute; import again later to update what is there, deciding every value E1 already holds yourself.
roles: The Import data permission in the project (Project administrator and Lead engineer have it) and the permissions of the changes the import makes

training.topic: Importing tag lists and data sheets from Excel

title: Import a P&ID from CAD (DXF)
summary: Bring a P&ID drawn in CAD into a project as objects on a 2D space: blocks become objects of the class they are named for or look like, lines become connected pipes and signals; import again to update.
roles: The Import data permission in the project (Project administrator and Lead engineer have it) and the permissions of the changes the import makes

title: Import a P&ID from a PDF
summary: Bring a P&ID exported from CAD as a PDF into a project: E1 finds its symbols, groups and recognizes them by their look, takes the texts beside them as tags and the line numbers as pipelines, and draws them connected on a 2D space.
roles: The Import data permission in the project (Project administrator and Lead engineer have it) and the permissions of the changes the import makes

training.topic: Importing a P&ID from a PDF

title: Save an import mapping and export with it
summary: Keep the mapping you reviewed in the import wizard under a name: the next workbook of the same shape maps itself, and File → Export with a saved mapping… writes the project's objects back in the same sheets, headers and units.
roles: Saving a mapping: Import into the project. Exporting: Export (Viewer and above)
